editorial.brief: ComfyUI was the only topic to show up on more than one feed today, appearing on GitHub trending and Hugging Face, where the image model flux-3-image-klein-comfy leads with 439,528 downloads. Elsewhere, Kim Jong Un topped Wikipedia on 321,739 views, ahead of Jailer 2 by a ratio of 1.1 to one. Nothing else connected.
editorial.cover_sub: Kim Jong Un topped Wikipedia with 321,739 views, ahead of Jailer 2 by a margin of 1.1 to one, on a day when the other feeds were busy with image models, a Knicks banner and the Fed.
editorial.wiki_deck: Kim Jong Un drew 321,739 views, narrowly ahead of Jailer 2 on 303,129. Nothing else in the snapshot says why.
editorial.letter_headline: One crossover, and the rest scattered
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News plays with a permit-bound SimCity at 669 points. Lemmy's top post, at 908, is a statement of fatigue. Bluesky splits between a Knicks banner and Brazilian politics, while Mastodon fretted over voting machines.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire ran on AI, from a US STEM pledge to a McDonald's pricing suit, while Britain searched Cyberpunk 2077 update 2.5 and Brazil searched pix 5 mil mei.
editorial.markets_deck: Flávio Bolsonaro leads Brazil's presidency market at 81%, the Fed stands pat at 88%, Bayern Munich win tonight at 46% and a Republican sweep sits at 9%.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,205,009 players on Steam, ahead of Dota 2 at 907,099 and PUBG at 778,436. On Twitch, caseoh_ drew 63,087 viewers, TheBurntPeanut 39,550 and supertf 10,577.
editorial.yt_note: A Minecraft speedrun finale leads at 1,532,078 views, followed by a Santa Fe Klan video on 933,655. Below that sit a Marvel Rivals trailer, an Honest Trailers Spider-Man and a BloodHound Q50 video.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow the 1.1x margin between Kim Jong Un and Jailer 2 will have reshuffled, the Knicks banner will be raised, Bayern will have a result, and the Fed odds will have moved a little. ComfyUI may still be trending, and the number 4 will still be 4.
wiki_paras: Kim Jong Un was the most-read article on Wikipedia in the latest daily count, with 321,739 views. Jailer 2 followed on 303,129, Elizabeth Holmes on 253,155, You Can See Everything on 206,507 and Helen Haines on 158,924. The top five span a little over 162,000 views.

The lead over second place is 18,610 views, a ratio of 1.1 to one. That is close enough that a slow afternoon in either direction would have swapped them. The snapshot offers no matching story on Hacker News, Lemmy, Bluesky or Mastodon, so the cause stays with whoever was reading.

Three of the five entries are people, and none of them has a counterpart elsewhere in the snapshot. The one topic that did cross feeds was ComfyUI, a GitHub project, which Wikipedia ignored. The encyclopedia and the rest of the web were reading different papers today.
letter_paras: The snapshot found one topic on more than one feed: Comfy-Org/ComfyUI, on GitHub trending and Hugging Face. Everything else ran on its own track. Kim Jong Un led Wikipedia, Counter-Strike 2 held Steam at 1,205,009 peak players, and the social feeds argued about different things. A scattered day, with a single thin thread through it.

In the quiet corners, the USGS logged 25 quakes of M2.5 or above in 24 hours, the largest an M5.4 near 192 km south of Burica, Panama. Cloudflare's busiest domains were plumbing: google.com, googleapis.com, cloudflare.com, gstatic.com, amazonaws.com. A Mastodon poster announced the random number 4, after the XKCD strip.

A same-hour snapshot removes the usual cheat of comparing a Tuesday morning in one feed with a Wednesday night in another. Every feed was read in the same minute, so when two agree, they agree about the same moment. When they do not, that disagreement is also a result, and today it is most of the page.
